hook.text: 12,900 years ago, the warming climate suddenly reversed. Temperatures plunged back to ice age levels.

buildup.text: The Younger Dryas lasted 1,200 years—a brutal cold snap just as humans were settling into warmer ways.

discovery.text: A likely trigger: meltwater from glaciers disrupted the Atlantic ocean current that warms Europe.

twist.text: This shock may have pushed Near Eastern groups toward farming—the cold forced new survival strategies.

climax.text: When the Younger Dryas ended abruptly 11,700 years ago, the stable warmth of our era finally began.

punchline.text: One last freeze may have sparked agriculture.

quiz.question: What was the Younger Dryas?
options: A sudden cold snap that interrupted post-ice-age warming
